why.heading: Why Shraddha Matters
why.intro: Shraddha is the tradition of remembering departed loved ones and ancestors with respect. It is an occasion for remembrance and gratitude, not for fear or grief.
why.whatBody: The word Shraddha is connected to श्रद्धा, reverence. Families offer water, food and service in memory of those who have passed. In many families this includes Tarpan, Pind Daan, Brahmin Bhojan and giving to others.
why.pakshaBody: Pitra Paksha is the waning-moon fortnight that follows Bhadrapada Purnima and ends on Sarva Pitru Amavasya. Purnimanta calendars place it in the month of Ashwin; Amanta calendars place it in Bhadrapada. It usually falls in September–October.
why.valuesTitle: Four feelings at the heart of it

values.label: Reverence
values.meaning: The respect in one’s heart with which the rite is performed.

values.label: Remembrance
values.meaning: Recalling the lives, the affection and the lessons of our loved ones.

values.label: Gratitude
values.meaning: Thankfulness for the values, family and life our ancestors gave us.

values.label: Service
values.meaning: Offering food, charity or help to someone in need, in their memory.

why.bhojanBody: Traditionally, a sattvic meal is cooked at home on the day of Shraddha, and a Brahmin is fed with respect and offered dakshina. Many families also set aside a portion of food for cows, crows, dogs and ants.
why.todayBody: It connects generations. Families sit together and remember grandparents and parents, and children learn the names and stories of those who came before them.
why.note: Shraddha rituals and dates differ between families, regions and traditions. Please seek guidance from your family priest or a qualified Acharya.

tradition.heading: परंपरा वही, तरीका नया।
tradition.headingNote: The tradition stays the same. The way we keep it has changed.
tradition.earlierBody: On the day of Shraddha, families invited a Brahmin home, cooked with love, and offered the meal in memory of their departed loved ones.
todayItems: Family members often live far from home, in different cities.
Busy schedules leave little time to prepare.
Many people do not know their loved one’s correct Shraddha Tithi.
It is unclear whom to contact for Brahmin Sewa.
Yet everyone wants the Sewa done with respect and in the right way.
tradition.closing: Pitra Sewa helps make this whole process simpler.

finderPage.metaDescription: Find your loved one’s Pitru Paksha Shraddha date from the date, time and place of death — with the Panchang convention shown and priest verification available.
finderPage.heading: Find Your Loved One’s Shraddha Date
finderPage.intro: From the date, time and place of death we find the Tithi of death using the Panchang, then the day of that Tithi in Pitru Paksha of the year you choose.
finderPage.privacy: Your details are used only for this calculation and are not stored by us.
finderPage.preliminary: The Panchang calculation is under review. For now, treat every result as final only after a priest confirms it.

result.heading: Your Shraddha Date
result.serviceErrorTitle: The Panchang service did not respond
result.serviceErrorBody: Please try again shortly. Meanwhile, you can print this slip and ask your priest.
result.notFoundBody: The date is outside the supported range. Please request a priest’s confirmation.

reasons.time-unknown: The time of death is not known and the Tithi changed that day, so more than one Tithi is possible. If death was before sunrise, the previous day’s Tithi is also possible.
reasons.near-boundary: The time of death is only {minutes} minutes from a change of Tithi.
reasons.sources-disagree: A second Panchang source disagrees with this calculation.
reasons.secondary-failed: The second Panchang source could not be reached for a cross-check.
reasons.two-days: This Tithi touches the Aparahna of two days. By the rule, the day with the larger share of Aparahna is chosen. The other day: {date}.
reasons.no-aparahna: This Tithi does not fall in any day’s Aparahna; by the rule, the day of the next Aparahna after it is chosen.
reasons.adhik-maas: An Adhik Maas falls within the calculation period.
reasons.purnima: For a death on Purnima, many families observe Shraddha on Bhadrapada Purnima; some on Sarva Pitru Amavasya.
reasons.chaturdashi: Many traditions keep Pitru Paksha Chaturdashi for untimely deaths; for a natural death, many families observe Shraddha on Amavasya.
reasons.first-year: It has not yet been a year since the death. First-year Shraddha customs can differ.
reasons.old-clock: Before 1956 some cities (e.g. Mumbai, Kolkata) kept local clock time different from IST.
reasons.engine-preliminary: The Panchang calculation is still under review, so every result is marked for confirmation.
reasons.close-call: A difference of a few minutes in sunrise or the Tithi change could move the Shraddha to another day.

traditions: When the Tithi is not known, many families observe Shraddha on Sarva Pitru Amavasya.
Many families observe Shraddha for mothers on Navami (Matri Navami).
For accidents or untimely deaths, many traditions observe Shraddha on Chaturdashi.
result.disclaimer: This date is calculated using the selected Panchang convention and location. Please confirm the final Shraddha date with your family priest, especially when regional traditions or exceptional Tithis may affect the observance.
result.printFooter: Slip created on the Pitra Sewa website on {date}.
